There are two kinds of knowledge in this world.
One is called Planck knowledge.
That is, deep knowledge.
It's an understanding built through deep thought
and wrestling with the problem again and again,
a genuine understanding that has taken root in your mind,
You know what it is.
Why is that?
Another type is what we might call chauffeur knowledge.
In other words, it is only surface-level knowledge.
It is still better than knowing nothing.
It lets us chat with people from all walks of life
and sound like we know exactly what we are talking about.
We may even convince most people that we really know our stuff.
When we have not truly dug into a subject
it is easy to fool ourselves into thinking that we truly understand it.
The worst part is that
we may have been led astray right from the start
and then pass that misinformation on to others without even realizing it.
As Feynman once put it,
The first principle is this: you must never fool yourself.
Because you are the easiest person in the world to deceive.
The best way to avoid being misled
is to learn deeply and think critically.
The Feynman Technique turns what you have memorized
and turns it into Planck knowledge, one of the most effective learning tools.
Feynman realized early on
that knowing what something is called
is completely different from truly understanding it.
As a child, Feynman's father taught him
you can know what a bird is called
in every language,
but when it comes to the bird itself,
you may have learned nothing about it.
Building on this idea,
Feynman developed a
simple, practical learning method.
It only takes four steps.
Step one: Define your goal.
Your goal can be as big or as small as you like.
Grab a blank sheet of paper.
Write down what you want to learn.
This is where all effective learning begins.
Step two: Teach it to someone else.
Explain it in simple terms
to someone who has no idea about the subject.
Don't just memorize and repeat the original wording.
Explain it in your own words.
Step three: Identify what you're missing.
Any part you struggle to explain
or anything the other person doesn't understand
Those are the gaps in your understanding.
Step four: revisit the material and learn it again.
Go back to your study materials and address your knowledge gaps.
Focus on the areas you struggle with.
Keep going until you can explain them clearly and confidently.
So why is teaching others
more effective than learning on your own?
Research from Stanford University has found that
when you learn as if you were going to teach someone else,
your brain switches from passively receiving information
to actively reconstructing it.
You not only have to understand what it is,
but also why it works and how to explain it.
This deeper level of processing helps knowledge stick
Knowledge retention is far higher than with simple reading and note-taking.

你随意选择学习内容，可能会给自己带来
很多困难。与其随机选择
学习，不如寻找一个结构化的学习路径。
你可以参考我频道上的一个视频，
名为“面向绝对初学者的 Web 开发学习指南”。
它展示了一个简化的学习路线图，列出了你
需要学习的主要技能以及
学习顺序。你也可以参加一些
在线训练营课程，例如 FreeCodeCamp、Zero
to Mastery 或 Ania Kubów 的 12 小时
HTML、CSS 和 JavaScript 训练营。 遵循
预先设定的学习路径的好处在于，你会清楚地知道自己需要
学习什么以及何时学习。随着你一步步
前进，你可以看到自己的进步，并
感受到自己确实在取得进展。当你
沿着既定路径学习时，你可能会想要同时
学习多种内容，
以便更快地完成所有学习任务。但
这样做实际上会分散你的注意力，
使知识更难记住。
因此，第二个建议是不要试图一次性学习所有内容，
而是一次只专注于学习一个知识点。
我建议你专注于一个主题，直到
你感觉自己对基础知识有了相当的掌握。
至少在刚开始学习的时候是这样。例如，
假设你首先学习HTML，当你

构建一个非常基本的HTML网页后，你就可以开始
学习CSS了。这样，将来如果你
遇到不熟悉的HTML标签，

特定的标签技巧，第三点是：要成为积极的学习者。
不要只是被动地接受内容，坐在那里
看着老师讲解

取得进步的。相反，你应该尝试将
新知识与实际应用结合起来。

看视频一边跟着 Wes 的代码练习。

去看视频。这种尝试在
不看源代码的情况下创建刚刚学到的东西的方法，可以
很好地检验你
到底记住了多少，也能很快帮

In this video, I will present the main five takeaways from The 10x Rule, written by Grant Cardone.
The 10x Rule is about pure domination mentality, and how to be the alpha of the industry.
The overall main points that Grant Cardone makes regarding how to reach extreme amounts of success can be divided into two parts -
extreme 10x GOALS, and
extreme 10x ACTION.
There are a bunch of practical takeaways that can help you wake up from your slumber, and make you reach your full potential.
Let's see how.
Takeaway number 1: 10x goals bootstrap your success
Maybe you need to find a job, lose 40 pounds, or find the right partner.
Although these scenarios cover different areas of your life, they all have one thing in common:
The person who desires them is not there yet.
To achieve success, to accomplish your goals, often turns out to be much harder than first anticipated.
This is because people have a tendency to underestimate the time, energy
money and effort necessary to bring their projects to the point of success.
This is the reason why goals should be set MUCH higher than what you might be comfortable with.
Let's say my goal is to make a buttload of money. So I set the goal to be the reasonable amount of
$500,000, which would enable a decent level of living with a good home, good food, a nice vacation every once in a while, and
some of those lovely Thai massages once or twice a month!
But now, pretend that I would instead have set the targets at five million dollars. Now THAT is a buttload.
No matter what I end up achieving, if I miss my target, which goal would I rather come up short on?
You want a big margin of safety in order to bootstrap your success.
This is a trick that is being adopted within sports, and more specifically,
mental trainers use it regularly with their elite athletes.
The athletes set out to become number one - nothing else.
Now, this might not always be realistic for everyone, but that's not the point either.
The point is that the person's actions are then aligned with their 10x goal.
And if the goal turned out to be out of reach, hey, at least the athlete ended up in third place and succeeded to out-compete like
99.99% of all the other competitors.
This holds true in business, personal life or whatever.
Set targets so high that even if you would come up short you are still perceived as, and will be, a winner.
Takeaway number 2: 10x action is required
Again, the amount of time, energy, money and effort required to bring a project to success is oftentimes underestimated.
When the miscalculation of the effort required becomes obvious (and it will) and you hit a wall, one becomes visibly
disappointed and discouraged.
This causes you to incorrectly identify the problem as a wall that you can't smash through, and sooner or later,
you assume that the target is unattainable and
ultimately throw in the towel.
If you instead anticipate that the amount of work required would be of the 10x character,
some setbacks are to be expected, and those walls that you hit, will no longer be made out of concrete.
And if this would turn out to be false - that there were no major setbacks or black or gray swans, hey, lucky you!…

要点一：攀登财务自由之山 将
你的财务之旅想象成攀登一座山峰。 就像
